correctness.rationale: For a uniform permutation, k revealed arrows consist of closed cycles and n-k open paths, so completing them adds a uniform permutation of the open paths. Conditional specified-cycle counting distinguishes cycles wholly before k, fixed point (k), and cycles crossing k, giving Cov(C_n,I_k)=(k-1)/(k^2 binom(n,k)) exactly. Binomial bounds prove the two-term aggregate asymptotic; record-indicator independence and Stirling equidistribution give the correlation rate. Exact rational enumeration through n=9 and all k<=n<=200 harmonic identities independently corroborate these claims.

originality.rationale: The same-permutation cycle–record positional kernel and the concentration of total covariance at its terminal record are distinct from the known marginal Stirling equidistribution and from cycle-versus-inversion or fixed-point-versus-descent covariances. value.rationale: Classical Stirling statistics of random permutations have identical marginal laws but genuinely different joint behavior on one permutation. Determining an exact positive mixed covariance for every record position and showing localization to the final record answers a natural dependence question beyond one-dimensional equidistribution and provides a structural route through partially closed permutation cycles.
